newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan coffee exports jump in October/November.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan coffee exports jump in October/November.

text.p: Ugandan coffee exports rose sharply in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/September) compared to the same period the previous year, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Wednesday.

In a report for November, UCDA said cumulative exports for October and November stood at 776,261 60-kg bags valued at $59.4 million compared to 400,173 bags valued at around $47.6 million in the comparative period in 1995/96.
Coffee exports in November 1996 stood at a provisional total of 436,261 bags, up from 340,000 bags in October -- and up from 228,386 bags realised in November 1995.

The Authority said coffee activity fell in the month of November which is usually wet. However, procurement tentatively stood at 15,000 tonnes (250,000 60-kg) of FAQ (Fair Average Quality), up from 12,000 tonnes reported in the previous month.
UCDA attributed the relatively higher export volumes in October and November to high opening stocks and "the inverted market which discourages hoarding of stocks al all levels".
Opening stocks for 1996/97 were estimated at around 1.5 million 60-kg bags -- 850,000 bags from the farm level, 415,000 bags from processors and 230,000 bags from exporters.
UCDA said that despite the increase in total value of coffee, the realised unit value of export continued to drop from $1.31 per kg in October to $1.24 per kg in November.
The drop was due to oversupply in robusta coffee in the international market by South American and Asian countries who account for nearly 65 percent of world robusta production.
Some 88 percent of Ugandan exports are robustas.
Farm gate prices also continued to decline in line with lower global prices. However, relative to prices on the world market, Ugandan farmers received good prices, the report said.

"The good prices came as a result of heavy hedging done by exporters at a time when the prices were relatively good, competition associated with free market systems and removal by the government of the coffee stabilisation tax," UCDA said.

"On average, the prices of dry cherries ranged between 400 and 500 shillings per kg while those of FAQ (Fair Average Quality) and parchment ranged between 900-1,050 shillings and 1,120-1,250 shillings respectively," UCDA said.

"(In the same period) last year, average farmgate prices were 825 shillings for (lower grade) Kiboko dry cherries, 1,730 for FAQ and 1,265 for arabica parchment, hence a respective price fall," UCDA said.
